name: Venus Optics Laowa 65mm f/2.8 2x Ultra Macro APO (Nikon Z)

focus.motor: None. Manual focus, manual aperture ring (full-stop clicks), no electronic contacts.
focus.notes: Internal focusing: the length stays constant (Venus Optics; OpticalLimits). Long throw from 2:1 to infinity, reported as about 220° (OpticalLimits), about 240° (Dustin Abbott), about 260° (Amateur Photographer) and about 270° (Jonas Rask); the field is null because the figures differ. With no contacts there is no EXIF, no camera-controlled aperture and no focus-distance readout (OpticalLimits; Abbott). Abbott found peaking unreliable for precise portrait-distance focus, so use magnified view at longer distances. At 1:1–2:1, set the ring for the magnification you want and focus by moving the camera or a rail.

stabilization.notes: Native Z mount, so FTZ II does not apply. IBIS only, on the Z8 and Z5 II, and only if 65 mm is entered under Setup menu > Non-CPU lens data (Nikon Z8 manual: the data enables on-board VR for non-CPU lenses). The Z50 II has no IBIS for stills. At 1:1–2:1, shift (x/y) shake dominates and in-body VR helps little at these magnifications (general macro principle, not lens-specific testing); use flash or a tripod.

close_focus.effective_aperture_at_max_mag: About f/8.4 at 2:1 when set to f/2.8. Using N_eff ≈ N × (1 + m): f/5.6 at 1:1 and f/8.4 at 2:1. Amateur Photographer gives f/5.6 at 1:1 (−2 stops) and f/8 at 2:1 (−3 stops). The camera cannot show this value (no CPU); metering through the lens handles the exposure.
close_focus.notes:
MFD 17 cm from the image plane at 2:1 (Venus Optics; Neocamera). No published working distance was found from Venus Optics or any reviewer. Estimated free working distance at 2:1: about 50–55 mm, computed as 170 mm MFD − 16 mm Z flange − about 100 mm lens length (Venus Optics Φ57 × 100 mm; whether the Z version's length includes the mount was not confirmed). Abbott says 1:1 gives only 'a couple of extra centimetres' over 2:1, so roughly 70–75 mm at 1:1 (estimate). Internal focus means the barrel does not grow toward the subject. Remove the hood at close range to avoid shading the subject (Abbott).

Effective aperture, N_eff ≈ N × (1 + m), computed:
- At 1:1 (×2, −2 stops): f/2.8→f/5.6, f/4→f/8, f/5.6→f/11, f/8→f/16, f/11→f/22, f/16→f/32.
- At 2:1 (×3, −3.2 stops): f/2.8→f/8.4, f/4→f/12, f/5.6→f/17, f/8→f/24, f/11→f/33, f/16→f/48.

Amateur Photographer reports the same (f/5.6 at 1:1, f/8 at 2:1). Jonas Rask observed only about 1 stop of exposure loss at 2x on Fuji bodies. That conflicts with the formula and with AP, so treat it as anecdotal. OpticalLimits found the aperture slightly inaccurate: marked f/22 behaves closer to f/14–f/16 at distance.

quick.headline: Superb APO 2:1 macro for DX: sharp from f/2.8 with no measurable CA. At 2:1 every marked stop is three stops smaller, so shoot f/2.8–f/4 and stack.
quick.wide_open: Excellent centre and very good borders at f/2.8; extreme DX corners 'good' (OpticalLimits). Abbott: excellent across the frame at f/2.8. DCW: centre very good wide open, peaking at f/4; corners more average.

by_focal.wide_open_note: OpticalLimits (Fuji X APS-C): f/2.8 centre excellent, borders very good, corners good; f/4 outer field improves noticeably; f/5.6 superb across the frame (best); f/8 marginal diffraction impact; f/16 still impressive. DCW (Canon EF-M lab): centre peak at f/4. AP (26MP X-T3): sharpest about f/5.6, visible softening beyond f/8.

quick.close_up_best: 1:1: f/4–f/5.6 set (f/8–f/11 effective). 2:1: f/2.8–f/4 set (f/8.4–f/12 effective) for maximum detail; f/5.6 (about f/17 effective) only when one frame must carry more depth.
quick.close_up_note: No source measured resolution at 1:1 or 2:1, so this is calculated. OpticalLimits saw marginal diffraction loss from f/8 at distance (APS-C), and Amateur Photographer saw softening 'almost immediately' at high magnification because effective apertures are small. Jonas Rask advises at least f/5.6 at 2x for usable depth of field and calls f/2.8 at 2x nearly useless (depth thinner than a hair). Best compromise: focus-stack at f/2.8–f/4 at 2:1 on the Z8's DX crop.
quick.diffraction_note: OpticalLimits (APS-C, distance): marginal impact at f/8, still impressive at f/16 (the marked f/22 is really about f/14–f/16). AP (26MP APS-C): visible softening beyond f/8. At 2:1 that onset (about f/8 effective) arrives at set f/2.8. On the Z8 DX crop (4.35 µm pitch) and Z50 II (about 4.2 µm), expect the same.
avoid: Do not shoot FX image area on the Z8 or Z5 II: it is an APS-C lens (set Image area to DX manually; with no CPU the body cannot detect it).
Avoid set f/8 and smaller at 2:1 (f/24+ effective) except as a last resort.
Do not shoot into the sun without care: flare-prone (Abbott).
quick.confidence_reason: One lab test (OpticalLimits, APS-C, verbal grades; values only in charts) plus DCW lab (centre peak f/4) and AP agree on f/4–f/5.6 at distance. Nothing measured at 1:1 or 2:1, and no working-distance figure is published, so the macro guidance is computed (low confidence on those parts).

character.bokeh: Generally good. OpticalLimits and Canon News: smooth foreground blur, harsher-edged background blur; highlights nice at f/2.8 with a hint of an outer ring, edgier and outlined at f/4–f/5.6 (blades not rounded at smaller apertures). Abbott: good with character, busy backgrounds acceptable, APO edge hardness mild. Rask and AP: creamy, beautifully blurred backgrounds.
character.flare_sunstar: Abbott: 'somewhat flare prone', with ghosting and veiling into the sun and a noticeable loss of contrast in backlit portraits. Sunstars not tested by any source found.
character.ca: APO: OpticalLimits found lateral CA practically non-existent and no axial CA (LoCA), which it calls unusual. Abbott: no visible LoCA even in high-contrast scenes. AP: no objectionable fringing of either kind. DCW: very well controlled.
character.distortion: Virtually none (OpticalLimits, without correction; DCW 0.17%; Abbott very low).
character.vignetting: Low: OpticalLimits about 0.7 EV wide open, fading by about f/5.6. Abbott: mild but extends well into the frame (+33 LR). AP: disappears in the macro range or at f/4.
character.coma_astro: Not tested; not an astro lens.
character.focus_breathing: Not measured. Internal focus, and strong breathing is inherent to going from infinity to 2:1.
character.other: OpticalLimits scores: optics 9, build 7.5, price/performance 9. All metal, not weather sealed. About 100mm-equivalent field of view on DX (Venus Optics). Z version released February 2021 (Nikon Rumors).

field_tips: Mount it, then set Image area to DX on the Z8/Z5 II and select the stored 65 mm f/2.8 Non-CPU lens data (for IBIS and EXIF).
At 2:1 the subject sits only about 5 cm from the front (estimate): take the hood off, light from the side or use a diffused flash.
Remember the hidden light loss: 2 stops at 1:1 and about 3 stops at 2:1. f/4 set is about f/8 at 1:1 and f/12 at 2:1.
For the sharpest 2:1 frames, shoot f/2.8–f/4 and focus-stack by rocking the camera or using a rail. Use f/5.6 only when one frame must carry more depth.
Expect no CA (APO) but watch flare: shade the front element when the sun is near the frame.

body_notes.note: Use DX crop (19.4MP, 4.35 µm): diffraction appears from about f/8 effective, which is set f/4 at 1:1 and set f/2.8 at 2:1. IBIS only with Non-CPU lens data; DX crop is not automatic with a contactless lens.

DX crop is about 11MP (computed from 6048 × 4032 /1.5²), with coarse pixels that tolerate smaller apertures (set f/5.6 at 2:1 is fine per pixel), but there is little to crop. IBIS needs Non-CPU lens data.
The natural body: native DX, 20.9MP (about 4.2 µm), about 100mm-equivalent framing. No IBIS, so use flash or a tripod at 1:1–2:1. Whether the Z50 II offers Non-CPU lens data was not verified.

sources.name: OpticalLimits: Laowa 65mm f/2.8 2x Ultra Macro APO review
sources.tested_on: Fujifilm X APS-C body (model/MP not stated on the page)
sources.findings: 335 g, 57 × 100 mm, 52 mm, 9 blades, f/2.8–f/22 full-stop clicks, MFD 0.17 m, 2:1, 14/10 with 3 ED, internal focus, about 220° throw. Resolution (verbal; numbers only in charts): f/2.8 centre excellent, borders very good, extreme corners good; f/4 outer field noticeably better; f/5.6 superb across the frame (best); f/8 marginal diffraction; f/16 still impressive; f/22 more than usable because the true aperture is about f/14–f/16. Field curvature negligible. Distortion virtually none. Vignetting about 0.7 EV wide open. Lateral CA practically none; no axial CA. Bokeh: nice f/2.8 highlights with a slight outer ring, outlined at f/4–f/5.6; smooth foreground, harsher background; blades not curved stopped down. No close-up resolution figures. Scores 9 / 7.5 / 9.

sources.name: Dustin Abbott: Laowa 65mm F2.8 Ultra 2x Macro Review
sources.tested_on: Sony a6500 (24MP APS-C) and a7RIII in APS-C mode
sources.findings: Excellent across the frame at f/2.8 with little centre-to-corner fall-off; better at f/4 and f/5.6 (one of the best APS-C results he has seen). No visible LoCA. Bokeh good with character. 'Somewhat flare prone': ghosting and veiling into the sun, contrast loss in backlight. Vignetting mild but extends into the frame (+33). Distortion very low. About 240° throw (0.37 m to infinity per his note). MFD 17 cm at 2:1; 1:1 gives 'a couple of extra centimetres' of working distance over 2:1. Remove the hood at close range. No electronics: no EXIF, no focal length to IBIS. Peaking unreliable for precise portrait focus.

sources.name: Amateur Photographer: Laowa 65mm f/2.8 2x Ultra Macro review
sources.findings: Effective aperture drops two stops at 1:1 (to f/5.6) and three stops at 2:1 (to f/8). About 260° focus travel from infinity to 17 cm. Wide open resolves impressive detail across the frame; sharpest about f/5.6 at longer distances, visible softening beyond f/8. At high magnification, diffraction softening is visible almost immediately. No objectionable lateral or longitudinal CA. Distortion essentially absent. Vignetting slight wide open, gone in the macro range or at f/4. Bokeh beautifully blurred. 'Sublime'.

sources.name: Digital Camera World: Laowa 65mm f/2.8 2x Ultra Macro APO review
sources.tested_on: Canon EF-M body (model/MP not stated in text)
sources.findings: Lab: centre very good wide open through f/11, excellent peak at f/4; corners more average than expected. Per-aperture lw/ph values only in chart images. CA very well controlled at all apertures. Distortion 0.17. 9 blades, f/22 min, MFD 0.17 m. Verdict: 'ludicrously sharp' for the price; best on a tripod.

sources.name: Jonas Rask: The Laowa 65mm f/2.8 2x Ultra Macro APO review
sources.findings: About 270° throw from 2x to infinity. In macro, use at least f/5.6; at 2x f/2.8 is 'about as useless as it gets' because the depth of field is thinner than a hair. Needed about 1 stop of extra exposure at 2x (observation, conflicts with AP). Creamy, pleasing out-of-focus areas.

sources.name: Canon News: Laowa 65mm f/2.8 2x Ultra Macro APO review (summary of OpticalLimits)
sources.findings: Centre tack sharp at f/2.8, slight corner softness; f/5.6 'as good as it gets'. Lateral and axial CA and distortion non-existent. Bokeh good; background blur could be better; blades not curved stopped down. Not an independent test.

sources.name: Venus Optics: Laowa 65mm f/2.8 2X Ultra-Macro APO product page
sources.findings: APS-C format, 65mm f/2.8, 24.4° AOV, 14/10 with 3 ED, 9 blades, MFD 17 cm, 2:1, Φ57 × 100 mm, 335 g, 52 mm filter, internal focus keeps length constant, Nikon Z among mounts. No working distance, image circle or throw stated.

sources.name: Neocamera spec page (Nikon Z version) and Nikon Rumors Z-mount release post
sources.findings: Neocamera: Z version 335 g, 57 × 100 mm, 52 mm, MFD 17 cm from the imaging plane, 2X, 9 blades, f/2.8–f/22, APS-C, internal focus, introduced 2021-02-19. Nikon Rumors (https://nikonrumors.com/2021/02/19/juts-released-laowa-65mm-f-2-8-2x-ultra-macro-apo-for-nikon-z-mount.aspx/amp): Z version 'just released' 2021-02-19, optimised for APS-C mirrorless.

sources.name: Nikon Z8 Online Manual: Non-CPU Lens Data
sources.findings: Setup menu: record focal length and maximum aperture for a non-CPU lens to enable features normally reserved for CPU lenses, including on-board vibration reduction.

chris_frost.summary: No Christopher Frost review of the Laowa 65mm f/2.8 2x Ultra Macro APO was found. A search with his name, a youtube.com-restricted search and an exact-title search returned only Dustin Abbott, Digital Camera World, OpticalLimits, Fstoppers and others. Nothing is attributed to him.

research_notes: 1) Every test was on Fuji X, Sony APS-C or Canon EF-M bodies (24–26MP APS-C). That matches the Z8 DX crop (19.4MP, 4.35 µm) and Z50 II (20.9MP) closely, so the verdicts transfer well, if anything slightly conservatively. No Nikon Z-specific test was found. 2) Working distance: no manufacturer or measured figure was found. 50–55 mm at 2:1 is computed from MFD (170 mm), Z flange (16 mm) and the 100 mm listed length. It assumes the 100 mm is measured from the mount and that the Z version keeps the same length, neither of which was confirmed. The 1:1 value is only inferred from Abbott's remark. Both are estimates, so working_distance_mm_at_max_mag is null. 3) Effective aperture: the formula N × (1 + m) agrees with Amateur Photographer (f/5.6 at 1:1, f/8 at 2:1). Jonas Rask's about-1-stop observation conflicts and is treated as anecdotal; pupil magnification for this lens is not published. 4) Focus throw: four figures between 220° and 270°, so null. 5) Rounded blades: AP says the diaphragm is curved; OpticalLimits and Canon News say it is not curved at smaller apertures. Null. 6) FX coverage: Venus Optics specifies APS-C. No test of the FX image area was found, so behaviour in FX mode is not documented here. Auto DX crop needs the lens to identify itself, which a contactless lens cannot (inference), so set DX manually. 7) Lens-cwi.pages.dev lists 12 blades and a 62 mm filter in its text, contradicting the manufacturer; it was ignored. 8) Close-up best apertures are computed from the f/8 diffraction onset (OpticalLimits, AP) and the effective-aperture factor. Low confidence.
